findings.title: Unpinned package executed on every start: brightspace-mcp-server
findings.detail: 'brightspace-mcp-server' launches brightspace-mcp-server through npx without a version. The client resolves the version at start time, so any future publish to that package name runs with your credentials. This is how postmark-mcp (Sept 2025) reached roughly 300 organisations.
findings.remediation: Pin an exact version and an integrity hash: "args": ["brightspace-mcp-server@<version>"] and drop the -y flag. Re-pin deliberately, after reviewing the diff.

findings.title: Description reads as instructions to the model (p=1.00): download_course_files
findings.detail: The description of 'brightspace-mcp-server.download_course_files' scores 1.00 on the instruction-detection model, and carries intent signals: concealment. Descriptions are documentation for a human, but they are delivered to the model as trusted context, so text that tells the model what to do is an attack surface rather than a description. The score is driven mainly by: concealment, cross_tool, log_len, entropy.

evidence.description: Download every file in a course's Content area to a folder on the host computer, in sub-folders named after the course's modules. Use this when the user wants a whole course (or one module) saved, instead of calling download_file once per file. Ask the user where to save it before calling; never guess a directory. It is safe to run again: files already on disk are skipped by default, so a rerun fetches only what is new and never overwrites the user's annotated copies. Use dryRun first to preview

findings.remediation: Read the description against what the tool actually does. If the text is legitimate, it usually means the tool should not have to instruct the model at all - move the guidance into the parameter descriptions or the server's own docs.

evidence.description: Fetch the content tree for a course showing modules, topics, files, and links. Use this when the user asks about course materials, lecture slides, uploaded files, content structure, or what's in a course module. Use moduleTitle to filter to a specific module (e.g. 'Labs', 'Staff', 'Homeworks') instead of fetching the entire tree. Use maxDepth to limit recursion depth for a table-of-contents view. A module or topic that isn't currently available carries isAvailable/availabilityStatus/availability

findings.remediation: Read the description against what the tool actually does. If the text is legitimate, it usually means the tool should not have to instruct the model at all - move the guidance into the parameter descriptions or the server's own docs.

findings.title: Toxic flow within 'brightspace-mcp-server': reads credentials or secrets + sends email or messages
findings.detail: 6 combination(s) exist where one tool reads credentials or secrets and another sends email or messages. Neither tool is malicious on its own; together they reads credentials and can send mail. This is the postmark-mcp shape: the mail tool was legitimate, the credentials were reachable, and the combination was the incident. Both sides live in the same server, which may well be by design; confirm it.
findings.remediation: Break the path, not the tools: scope the credential so the source tool cannot reach anything valuable, or require explicit user confirmation on the sink tool (destructiveHint / human-in-the-loop), or split the two capabilities across trust boundaries that cannot share a context window.

findings.title: No baseline supplied - drift detection is disabled
findings.detail: Without an approved snapshot the scanner cannot tell a tool that has always been there from one that appeared yesterday. The single most effective MCP control is the diff, and it needs a baseline to diff against.
findings.remediation: Run 'mcp-scrutiny baseline --config <file> --out mcp-baseline.json', commit the file, and pass it back with --baseline on every later scan.
